definition: Visual symbols of the Akan people of Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire. Each one carries a proverb or idea, printed on cloth, carved, and stamped.
Members buy a share of a farm’s harvest before the season starts, then receive produce as it comes in. The farm gets money up front; members share the risk.
A crop planted mainly to protect and feed the soil between harvests, not to sell. Clover, rye, and vetch are common.
A fermented seasoning made from African locust beans, used across West Africa for deep, savory flavor.
Fujifilm’s built-in color and tone profiles, each modeled on one of its film stocks, like Classic Chrome or Eterna.
A set of camera settings layered on a film simulation to get a specific look straight out of the camera.
also: simulation recipes, simulation recipe, film recipes

definition: A tiny grain from the millet family, grown across West Africa’s Sahel for thousands of years. It cooks in about five minutes and grows in poor, dry soil.
Whether people can reliably reach and afford enough healthy food where they live.

The right of communities to decide their own food and farming systems, with healthy, culturally fitting food grown in ways that care for the land. The term comes from La Via Campesina, a global farmers’ movement.
The area food travels from to reach a place, like a watershed for food. Mapping one shows how much a region could feed itself.
A Bakongo symbol of a cross inside a circle. It traces the cycle of life through the four moments of the sun, and the line between the living and the ancestors.
An Adinkra symbol of a twisting path. It stands for initiative, versatility, and staying with the journey.
A way to organize notes by Tiago Forte: Projects, Areas, Resources, and Archives.
Farming that aims to rebuild soil health and biodiversity, through practices like cover crops, less tilling, and rotational grazing. There’s no single official definition.
An Akan word and Adinkra symbol meaning “go back and get it”: learn from the past to move forward.
Spiced grilled meat from Northern Nigeria and Niger, coated in a peanut and pepper spice blend called yaji.
